Name the two modes of reproduction in plants.
questions.a: Asexual reproduction (new plants from roots, stems, leaves) and sexual reproduction (through flowers, seeds and fruits).

questions.q: What is vegetative propagation?
questions.a: Growing new plants from vegetative parts like the root, stem or leaf without seeds or flowers.

questions.q: Why do farmers prefer vegetative propagation for fruit trees?
questions.a: New plants are exactly like the parent, grow faster and bear fruit earlier than seed-grown trees.

questions.q: What is cross-pollination?
questions.a: Transfer of pollen from one flower to the stigma of another flower, often by insects, wind or water.

questions.q: How does self-pollination differ from cross-pollination?
questions.a: Self-pollination lands pollen on the same flower or same plant; cross-pollination carries it to another plant, mixing genes.

questions.q: Name two agents of pollination.
questions.a: Insects (bees, butterflies) and wind (also water, birds).

questions.q: What happens in the embryo sac during fertilisation?
questions.a: The male gamete fuses with the egg cell, forming a zygote that grows into the plant embryo.

questions.q: How is the zygote formed in plants?
questions.a: After the pollen tube reaches the ovule, the male gamete joins the egg - this fusion is the zygote.

questions.q: What does the zygote develop into?
questions.a: It divides repeatedly to form the embryo inside the seed.

questions.q: What are oviparous animals? Give two examples.
questions.a: Animals that lay eggs outside their bodies - hens, frogs, snakes, fish.

questions.q: What are viviparous animals?
questions.a: Animals that give birth to live young which grow inside the mother's body, like cows, dogs and humans.

questions.q: Why do egg-laying animals lay many eggs?
questions.a: Eggs laid outside face predators and weather, so laying in numbers lets some young survive.

questions.q: What is metamorphosis?
questions.a: The big change in body form as a young animal grows into an adult, like tadpole to frog.

questions.q: Name an insect that undergoes metamorphosis and name its stages.
Why must a tadpole live in water but a frog can live on land?
questions.a: The tadpole breathes by gills and swims; the adult frog develops lungs and limbs for life on land.

questions.q: How does yeast reproduce asexually?
questions.a: By budding - a small outgrowth (bud) grows on the parent cell, splits off and becomes a new yeast.

questions.q: How do hydra and yeast show budding?
questions.a: Hydra grows a bud on its body that breaks away as a new polyp; yeast cells form tiny buds that separate.

questions.q: Name two other methods of asexual reproduction.
questions.a: Binary fission (amoeba, bacteria) and spore formation (fungi, ferns); also fragmentation and regeneration.
